name: Jurkovič Villa
known: The gallery's separate 2025 financial report gives CZK 168.5M in total, with CZK 116.9M as the founder's operating contribution and CZK 24.2M in earmarked founder funds.
Branch of the Moravian Gallery in Brno, a state museum founded by the Ministry of Culture.

name: Villa Tugendhat
known: In 2025 the museum's founder, the City of Brno, gave it CZK 108,278 thousand, of which CZK 1,229 thousand was returned.

name: Bauer Villa
known: The foundation was founded by the lawyer Pavel Šafář, who offered the collection to the state in 2016 (Culturenet, Aktuálně.cz).

name: Semler Residence
known: Budget, founder contribution and visitor numbers are in the Gallery of West Bohemia's 2024 report.

name: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art
known: Founded by Leoš Válka with his business partner Robert Aafjes.
Janeček co-founded the algorithmic trading company RSJ (English Wikipedia).

name: Galerie Rudolfinum
known: Director in 2025: Julia Bailey (gallery annual report 2025).
Abakus, the foundation of the Avast founders Pavel Baudiš and Eduard Kučera (abakus.cz), is the gallery's long-term sponsor (annual report 2025); the partners page lists Abakus as Gallery Partner.
The director's foreword thanks the Members and Patrons of the Galerie Rudolfinum Club, sponsors, partners and the Ministry of Culture (annual report 2025).
An advisory committee first met in 2025; it includes a curator, Helena Musilová, representing the Ministry of Culture (annual report 2025).

name: Kunsthalle Praha
known: Founded by the collectors Petr and Pavlína Pudil through The Pudil Family Foundation.
Director: Ivana Goossen.
The Pudil Family Foundation pays for the project and states it uses no public money (founders' letter, foundation annual report 2023).
Petr Pudil is a co-founder of BPD Partners, a firm with interests in property development and agrarian chemicals (The Art Newspaper).

name: National Gallery Prague
known: The Ministry of Culture, the gallery's founder, contributed 387.9 million CZK to running costs in 2024, 3.5 percent more than in 2023, plus 46 million CZK in subsidies, 30.4 million of it for capital spending (annual report 2024).
A public call by artists and 23 advisory-board resignations in June 2024 criticised director Knastová.

name: Villa Bílek
known: On site: a long-term exhibition since 1 June 2022, curated by Martin Krummholz, with a model of Bílek's Žižka Monument in the largest first-floor room.

In 2024 the gallery received a non-investment contribution of CZK 122,756.6 thousand and an investment contribution of CZK 164,504.6 thousand from its founder, which the atlas record names as the City of Prague.

name: Bata Villa (Thomas Bata Foundation)
known: Bata Schuh Stiftung, listed as founder, gave CZK 4,396,860.
Bata, chaired the Zlín board from 1998 to 2012 and then chaired the Bata Shoe Foundation.

Overlaps: Zlín's mayor Jiří Korec and Continental Barum's HR director Petr Dostál sit on the board, and on 16 August 2025 the Foundation lent the villa garden to Continental Barum for a rally stage (2025 report).
Its 2025 report lists Bata Schuh Stiftung as founder.
Rosemarie Bata Blyth chairs the board, which includes Zlín's mayor.

name: Zikmund Villa
known: In 1942 the film director Elmar Klos bought it.
Vančura owns the villa and chairs the foundation board (villa's site).
He co-founded the forge Kovárna VIVA in 1992 (Czech Wikipedia).
Board links: the vice-chair Jaroslav Juráš is shown on the foundation's site with the law office Juráš a partneři, which is also a donor.

Run by Nadační fond Zikmundova vila, founded in 2020 by the owner Čestmír Vančura, who chairs its board; the vice-chair, lawyer Jaroslav Juráš, is tied on the foundation's site to the law office Juráš a partneři, also a donor.
The foundation files annual reports for 2022 to 2025 and accounts for 2020 and 2021 in the public court register; its site names its board and director, and the 2025 report lists donors and grants.

name: Fondation Donwahi
known: Donwahi is president and artistic director (CAAC;
The curator Simon Njami contributed to the reconstruction after 2011, and Marème Malong is vice president (C&).
Founded by a group of art lovers, mostly African private-sector figures (C&, 2019).
